newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Novartis shares start Swiss trading.
newsitem.headline: Novartis shares start Swiss trading.

text.p: Shares in Novartis, the company formed by the merger of Swiss pharmaceutical groups Ciba-Geigy AG and Sandoz AG, began trading on the Swiss Exchange for the first time on Monday.
Trade started at 1,502 Swiss francs per share for both of Novartis' classes, bearer and registered shares.
The mega-merger of Ciba and Sandoz created the world's biggest pharmaceutical company after Britain's Glaxo-Wellcome.
Novartis has 4.4 percent of the world's fragmented pharmaceutical market based on 1995 sales while Glaxo-Wellcome had 4.7 percent.
Shares in Ciba and Sandoz traded for the last time on Friday, Dec 20.
Ciba's registered shares in Ciba ended at 1,595 francs and the registered shares of Sandoz ended at 1,494 francs.
